handoff: Harness sh() bound is correct and its regression test is green, but it covers only the harness's own git calls. In-process norn git calls (store gitSync, local subcommands unbounded per H11) and direct spawnSync in test files can still hang the tier, including reproduce's top suspect for the CI hang. F1 blocking: add a bound the harness controls (tier watchdog or test-only in-process git timeout) plus a red-first fixture test. F2 minor: the timeout kills git only, so its grandchildren are orphaned.

findings.title: In-process norn git calls (and direct spawnSync in tests) can still hang the tier
findings.detail:
Spec Wanted: 'The integration tier never hangs past the per-test timeout. A stuck test fails within its 20s with its name in the log.' The fix bounds only test/support/harness.ts sh(). The harness runs commands in-process via runCli (test/support/harness.ts:4, :388), so a command's local git calls use gitSync → spawnSyncCaptured with timeoutMs undefined (gitTimeoutMs returns undefined for local subcommands, git.ts:20-24). After the file's first spawnSync, bun 1.3.13 cannot cut that call, per reproduce's probe table. Reproduce's hypothesis 1 for the CI hang in upgrade-records.test.ts AC1 runs through norn upgrade's own git calls, not sh(). Direct Bun.spawnSync in test files is also unbounded (records.test.ts:217, story-reopen.test.ts:242, machine-dir.test.ts:215, herdr-plugin.test.ts:45). No test covers a stuck in-process git call.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Keep H11 for real runs. Add a bound the harness controls: a tier-level watchdog around test:integration that kills the run when output stops for longer than the largest per-test timeout and prints the files still running (this also covers the FIFO row), or a test-only timeout for in-process git under the harness. Add a fixture test like harness-git-timeout.test.ts in which an in-process norn git call sticks; it should go red today and green after the fix.

findings.title: Timeout kills only git, not its process group
findings.detail:
spawnSyncCaptured sends SIGKILL to the git pid only. A child git started (the fixture's alias `!sleep 60`, or a hook or ssh) is orphaned and keeps running until it exits. Output goes to files, so nothing blocks, but processes leak while the tier runs.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Acceptable as is. If F1's fix adds a watchdog, have it kill the whole process group.
